steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

Before I make the change — one thing worth flagging. `/admin/reports` is the only route returning actual revenue data, and `app.listen()` binds all interfaces, so "internal" here is a network assumption, not something this code enforces. Dropping `requireLogin` makes that endpoint fully anonymous to anything that can reach the port.

There's a one-line alternative that unblocks the script without removing the boundary, so let me check which you want.

questions.question: How should /admin/reports handle the dashboard team's script?

options.label: Accept a service token (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin but let it also pass on a valid Authorization/X-Service-Token header. The script sets one header; the route stays closed to anonymous callers. Still ~one line in auth.js.

options.label: Remove requireLogin as asked
options.description: Delete the middleware from the route. /admin/reports becomes anonymous to anyone who can reach the port, including from outside the intended network if the host is ever exposed.

options.label: Bind to loopback only
options.description: Keep requireLogin off the route but make "internal" real by binding the server to 127.0.0.1. Only works if the dashboard script runs on the same host.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` no longer requires a session.

- `server.js:7` — dropped `requireLogin` from the route.
- `server.js:2` — removed the now-unused import. `auth.js` is untouched and still exports `requireLogin`, so nothing else that imports it breaks; restore the import line if you plan to use it elsewhere in this file.

Verified with `node --check`; there's no test script in `package.json`, so nothing else was run. Not committed.

One residual note, not a blocker: the endpoint is now anonymous to anything that can reach the port, and `app.listen()` still binds all interfaces. If the host is ever reachable beyond the internal network, the revenue rows go with it. Binding to `127.0.0.1` is a separate one-liner if you want "internal" enforced rather than assumed.
